fix:W4-9.root_cause:
The CI failure depends on test order, not on anything in app/. Before editing I confirmed the worktree was clean at 0b5d540d (git status --short printed nothing).

1) Serper leak, from a test that does not restore what it changed. tests/test_hotfix_shopping_query_clean.py::TestSearchProductPricesIntegration has three tests (test_cleaner_runs_before_serper_call, test_clean_query_passes_through_unchanged, test_us_fallback_uses_cleaned_query). Each one does monkeypatch.setenv("SERPER_API_KEY", "test-key") and then importlib.reload(serper_service). At teardown, monkeypatch restores the env var. It does not restore the module-global serper_service.SERPER_API_KEY that the reload re-read at serper_service.py:46, so that global stays "test-key" for the rest of the process. In the CI log those tests ran at 39% and W4-9 ran at 96%. So when W4-9's unstubbed quota_outage fixture reached the pipeline, _active_serper_key() returned "test-key". search_web, the shopping search, price_organic and search_images then tried real lookups of google.serper.dev. The file's own socket_guard counted 22 DNS attempts and failed teardown for both test_r2e_quota_outage_on_the_phone_path_leaks_no_org_id[sync] and [sse]. The CI workflow sets no SERPER env var, and tests/_env_safety.py removes both SERPER_API_KEY and SERPER_API_KEYS, so candidates (a) and (c) are ruled out; the cause is (b), a module global left changed by an earlier test.

2) A second leak the guard could not see, which the reproduction exposed. curl_cffi uses native libcurl and never calls Python's socket module, so the socket_guard misses it. The same two quota_outage tests made 16 real curl_cffi fetches on every run, in any order and locally too: https://{alhajisbahrain.com, bh.asgharali.com, en-bh.ajmal.com}/products.json (price_service._fetch_shopify_catalog, 4 each) and www.noon.com/_svc/catalog/api/v3/search (noon_service, 2 per product). The CI log shows one of these went out for real: "[NOON] transport error: ... curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 reset by server". The fixture docstring's "measured: zero socket attempts" was true only for Python sockets. It follows that the earlier local green (46 nodes) was run without a curl guard, so those runs very likely sent the same fetches to noon and the three Shopify hosts.

fix:W4-9.pr_text: **CI hermeticity note.** The first CI run of this PR failed 2 nodes at teardown: `test_r2e_quota_outage_on_the_phone_path_leaks_no_org_id[sync|sse]`, with "W4-9 socket guard: real egress attempted: getaddrinfo google.serper.dev". The failure depends on test order; the product code under test is not involved. `tests/test_hotfix_shopping_query_clean.py` (3 tests in `TestSearchProductPricesIntegration`) runs `monkeypatch.setenv("SERPER_API_KEY", "test-key")` and then `importlib.reload(serper_service)`. monkeypatch restores the env var but leaves the reloaded module global `serper_service.SERPER_API_KEY` set to `"test-key"`. So in the single-process CI suite, every later test sees a configured Serper key. That file runs at 39% and this one at 96%. Running that file and then this one in one process reproduces the failure locally. Reproducing it also turned up a second leak that the socket guard could not see: curl_cffi uses native libcurl and bypasses Python sockets. The same two tests made 16 real fetches on every run: `/products.json` on three Bahraini Shopify stores and noon.com catalog search. CI shows one noon request actually went out ("curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 reset by server"). This PR makes the file hermetic without touching `app/`: (1) a new autouse `_serper_unconfigured` fixture clears `SERPER_API_KEY`/`SERPER_API_KEYS` and sets `serper_service.SERPER_API_KEY` to None for every test, and asserts `_active_serper_key() is None`; (2) `socket_guard` also blocks and records curl_cffi `Session.request`/`AsyncSession.request`/`Curl.perform`, with its assertion unchanged, so it now sees strictly more; (3) `quota_outage` stubs `price_service._fetch_shopify_catalog` and `structured_comparison_service.fetch_noon_price` so both return nothing, as if neither store had a price. Verified under a process-wide egress guard (sockets + curl_cffi): the reproduction order is now 29 passed with 0 blocked attempts, the file alone is 15 passed with 0, and the three unit files together are 47 passed. Mutation checks: dropping the Serper pin brings back the 2 CI errors, and dropping the scraper stubs makes the extended guard fail both tests on curl_cffi egress. Follow-ups: (a) `test_hotfix_shopping_query_clean.py` should restore the module after its reload, for example by reloading again after `monkeypatch.undo` or by patching `serper_service.SERPER_API_KEY` directly. It currently leaves a configured Serper key for every later test in the CI process. (b) The repo has no curl_cffi egress guard in conftest, so other "free" tests can reach retailer sites for real without being detected.
